texts.preamble: Smt. Olikee Kavitha vs The State Of Telangana on 31 October, 2023 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K. Lakshman Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt. Justice K. Sujana Writ Petition No.18112 Of 2023 Oral Order
texts.facts: This writ petition is filed to issue a writ of habeas corpus directing the respondents to produce detenu viz.,, Olikee Anjaneyulu S/o Olikee Chandraiah, now detained in Central Prison, Cherlapally, Medchal - Malkajgiri District, by setting aside the order of detention passed by respondent No.2 vide proceedings No.29/PD- CELL/CYB/2023, dated 12.05.2023, and the consequential confirmation order, if any, declaring it as illegal. 3. Respondent No.2 had passed the impugned detention order dated 12.05.2023 against the detenu under the provisions of Section - 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot- leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic KL,J & SKS,J Offenders Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short 'Act No.1 of 1986'), under the category of 'Goonda' as defined under Section - 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of 1986. 4. The impugned detention order was passed by respondent No.2 - detaining authority relying on five (05) crimes committed by the detenu in quick succession in the months of November and December, 2022 within a span of twelve (12) days in Medchal Police Station limits of Cyberabad Police Commissionerate. 5. Mr. Pothamshetti Manoj Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner, would submit that the impugned detention order was issued without application of mind. In all the ground cases, the bails were granted to the detenu. The detaining authority did not consider the entire material properly Smt. Olikee Kavitha vs The State Of Telangana on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179278851/ 1 including the role played by the detenu in the alleged crimes. The allegations levelled against the detenu will not fall under the category of 'goonda'. Even then, the detention order KL,J & SKS,J was passed which is illegal. Further, the apprehension of detaining authority that the detenu may commit similar offences and his acts would disturb 'public order' is baseless. Without considering all the said aspects, respondent No.2 passed the impugned order of detention which is illegal and, therefore, the same is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. The detaining authority, considering the entire material available on record and after arriving at the subjective satisfaction only, passed the detention order. Thus, there is no error in it. 7. Perusal of detention order dated 12.05.2023, grounds of detention, counter filed by respondent No.2 and the record would reveal that the detaining authority had passed the impugned detention order relying upon the five (05) crimes, which were committed in the recent past between November and December,2022, that too within a span of twelve (12) days viz., i) Crime Nos.929 of 2022, ii) 910 of KL,J & SKS,J 2022; iii) 915 of 2022; iv) 932 of 2022 and v) 933 of 2022, all registered by Medchal Police Station for the very same offences punishable under Sections - 457 and 380 of IPC. i) In Crime No.929 of 2022, the allegations levelled against the detenu and his associate are that on 08.12.2022 at around 2100 hours, the complainant left the Lord Hanuman Temple at Akbarjapet in Medchal locking it and returned on the next day at 0530 hours and found main gate lock and almirah were broke open and an amount of Rs.6,000/- missing from two hundis which were kept inside the almirah. According to the complainant, unknown persons gained entry into the said temple and committed theft of money from almirah. a) During investigation, on credible information, on 12.12.2022 at 0500 hours, the detenu along with his associate, accused No.2, were apprehended by the police. The detenu being accused No.1 admitted the guilt of commission of offence and other offences. The police recorded the confessional statement of the detenu, wherein he admitted that he and accused No.2 used to consume alcohol regularly and in order to meet their vices, both of them decided to commit thefts from hundis of temples located in the outskirts of villages. As per their plan, in the second week of December, 2022, during night hours, KL,J & SKS,J the detenu and accused No.2 went to Anjaneya Swamy Temple on his pulsar bike and the detenu instructed accused No.2 to stay outside the temple to watch the surroundings and alert if anyone comes from the outside. The detenu gained entry into the temple by breaking open the lock of temple and tried to break open the hundi's lock but failed. However, he broke open the almirah using an iron rod carried with him and committed theft of Rs.6,000/- from small hundi kept in the almirah and escaped from there. From the stolen amount, he had taken Rs.4,000/- as his share and the remaining amount of Rs.2,000/- was given to his associate - accused No.2. Smt. Olikee Kavitha vs The State Of Telangana on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179278851/ 2 b) In pursuance of the said confessional statement, the police seized one Bajaj Pulsar 150 CC bike bearing registration No.TS 35B 4474; Vivo Mobile from the possession of the detenu and later proceeded to your residence and recovered Rs.7,500/- cash of which, Rs.1,000/- pertains to the present case. Thereafter, the detenu was arrested by the police and he was sent to judicial custody. During test identification parade, the eye-witness identified the detenu and accused No.2 as the persons who committed the aforesaid offence. c) In this crime, the detenu was granted conditional bail. Though the police filed a petition seeking cancellation of bail, it was KL,J & SKS,J dismissed. After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer laid the charge sheet and the same was taken on file vide C.C. No.2301 of 2023. ii) While the investigation was in progress in Crime No.929 of 2022, the detenu admitted to have committed similar offences at different places vide Crime Nos.910 of 2022, 915 of 2022, 932 of 2022 and 933 of 2022. In all the said crimes also, the detenu was granted conditional bail and the police laid charge sheets and the same were taken on file vide C.C. Nos.2299 of 2023, 2300 of 2023; 2302 of 2023 and C.C. No.2303 of 2023, respectively. iii) Apart from the above five (05) crimes, the detenu is also involved in Crime No.937 of 2022 registered by the very same police for the very same offences. However, this crime was not relied upon by the detaining authority while passing detention order and only referred it. iv) The modus operandi adopted by the detenu and his associate is that they would identify temples located on the outskirts of villages at isolated places. After identifying them, they go to the targeted temple on bike and enter the temple by breaking open the KL,J & SKS,J door/gate of the temple with the iron rod carried by them, while the detenu was waiting outside the temple watching the surroundings to alert the associate of detenu about movement of people outside and surrounding the temple. The associate of the detenu would break open the Hundis and collect the cash from it and flew away from there with stolen booty and later share between them. 8. Thus, the aforesaid facts would reveal that the detenu and his associate, who is accused No.2 were repeatedly engaging in unlawful activities of committing theft of cash from the hundis of temples during night hours by breaking open locks of doors/gates of temples under the limits of Cyberabad Police Commissionerate and thereby causing panic and fear among general public and acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order' and thereby disturbs peace and tranquility in the area. 9. The detaining authority considering that the detenu involved in series of offences of theft of cash from the temple hundis in night hours and also the fact of pendency of petitions filed seeking cancellation of bails and that the detenu may commit similar offences in his limits in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public KL,J & SKS,J order' and the acts of the detenu terrorized all sections of people, fearing theft of money and valuables from the temples at the outskirts, passed the detention order. Thus, the said acts committed by the detenu Smt. Olikee Kavitha vs The State Of Telangana on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179278851/ 3 would certainly disturb the public order.
texts.arguments: 6. On the other hand, Mr. Mujib Kumar Sadasivuni, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of the respondents would submit that the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious and grave in nature. To prevent him from doing similar acts in future, respondent No.2 has passed the impugned order of detention. The object of the Act No.1 of 1986 is to provide for preventive detention of Bootleggers, Dacoits etc. including 'Goonda'. Section - 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of 2018 defines "Goonda", which means a person, who either by himself or as a member of or leader of a gang, habitually commits, or attempts to commit or abets the commission of offences punishable under Chapter XVI or Chapter XVII or Chapter XXII of the IPC. 12. It is not in dispute that the detaining authority shall consider the nature of offence and the manner in which it was committed. 13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration 1 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society. The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar 2, the Apex Court held as under: "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder. The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large. A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert Smt. Olikee Kavitha vs The State Of Telangana on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179278851/ 4 the public order are. It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order".
